title: Database moved to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
summary: The app's data now lives in a managed PostgreSQL database on Amazon RDS (Mumbai), separate from the app server. The app started with an empty database: the earlier test projects, floors and drawings were not carried over.

sections.heading: Setup
points: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 17, db.t4g.micro, 20 GB storage that grows automatically, encrypted.
Private: only the app server can reach it, nothing on the internet.
Its password is kept in AWS Parameter Store and never written anywhere else.
Deletion protection is on, and deleting the AWS setup leaves a final snapshot.

sections.heading: Backups
points: It can be restored to any minute within the last 1 day. The AWS Free plan doesn't allow longer; raise this to 7 days after upgrading the account plan.
Uploaded drawings, BBS and takeoff files are still on the server's data disk, with daily snapshots kept for 7 days.

sections.heading: Fresh start
points: Project Master starts empty. Add the real projects.
Users are created again when they first sign in. Admins are recognised from the admin email list; other users need their role set again in User Management.
The old test data (SQLite file and uploaded files) is kept aside on the server in /data/_sqlite_test_data_2026-11 until it's no longer needed.

sections.heading: Checked before the switch
points: Database migrations ran on PostgreSQL.
Sign-in, projects, floors, schedule, hindrances, drawings, users, roles and Version History all worked against a scratch copy, which was then deleted.

title: Version History page
summary: Admins can see what changed in the app and on which date, under Administration → Version History.

title: Database prepared for future growth
summary: The database stays on SQLite, but the app can now move to a managed database (Amazon RDS PostgreSQL) by changing one setting and copying the data once. The daily backups were tested by restoring one.

sections.heading: Where the data lives
points: All data is in one SQLite database file, /data/app.db, on the AWS server's separate data disk. Uploaded drawings, BBS and takeoff files sit on the same disk.
That disk survives server restarts and changes of server size.
AWS takes a snapshot of the disk every day and keeps the last 7.

sections.heading: What changed
points: Connection setting: the backend now accepts a DATABASE_URL, like a Spring datasource URL. If it is not set, the existing SQLite file is used, so nothing changes on AWS today.

Migrations: table changes are now versioned scripts (Alembic, the Python equivalent of Flyway) instead of hand-written start-up fixes. Version 0001 is the full schema as of November 2026. The app applies new versions by itself on start-up.
Data checks: SQLite now enforces links between tables, as Postgres always does.
Deleting a project that still has drawings is refused with a clear message.
Deleting a floor used in the quantity sheet or schedule is refused with a clear message.
Deleting a quantity-sheet activity that has quantities entered is refused with a clear message.
Deleting a schedule activity that has hindrances linked to it is refused with a clear message.

sections.heading: Backup restore test (10 Nov 2026)
points: The snapshot from 9 Nov 2026, about 3:16 am IST, was restored to a temporary disk and opened read-only. The live app kept running throughout.
The database passed the SQLite integrity check, with no broken links.
Projects (3), floors (27), users and roles matched the live data exactly.
The temporary disk was deleted afterwards.

sections.heading: When to move to RDS PostgreSQL
points: When more than one backend server is needed.
When many people save at the same moment.
When restore-to-the-minute is needed instead of last night's snapshot.
When reporting tools such as Power BI or Metabase need direct access.
Expected cost is very roughly $15–25 a month for the smallest size.

title: Renamed to "Operating System"
summary: "Operations Platform" now reads "Operating System" under the Global Buildestate logo in the sidebar, on the sign-in page and in the browser tab title.

title: Dashboard fits on phones
summary: The module cards on the Dashboard no longer overflow on phone screens.

sections.heading: Details
points: Cards have a fixed height, so the icon, name and "Open →" always fit.
There are 3 cards per row on desktop and 2 on phones, or 1 on very narrow screens.
Long module names wrap to two lines.
On small phones the welcome banner is more compact.

title: Drawing Register
summary: Each project keeps its current drawings in one place, with full revision history.

sections.heading: What it does
points: Upload PDF or DWG drawings, up to 100 MB each, with drawing number, name, discipline and remarks.
Revisions are numbered automatically R0, R1, R2 and so on. The newest is Current and older ones are kept as Superseded.
PDFs open in a new browser tab. For DWGs the server makes a picture of the drawing to preview.
Search by name or number, and filter by format and discipline.
Anyone whose role includes the Drawing Register module can view, download and upload.

title: Moved to AWS (Mumbai)
summary: The app is hosted on AWS in the Mumbai region and served over HTTPS at 13-205-5-179.sslip.io.

sections.heading: Details
points: One server runs the backend, with the website files served from the same address.
Data is on a separate disk that survives restarts, with daily snapshots kept for 7 days.
A reboot test on 30 Oct 2026 confirmed that Project Master data survives a restart.

title: Bar Bending Schedule (BBS)
summary: A bar bending schedule is generated from beam drawings (DWG). Laps and covers are taken from the drawing notes.

title: Quantity Takeoff
summary: Quantities are taken off from structural drawings (DWG) floor by floor, with AI assistance, and can be exported to Excel.

title: Project Schedule improvements
summary: Schedule rows can be grouped and linked to floors from Project Master.

title: Login, roles, Project Master, Project Schedule and Hindrance Register
summary: Users sign in with Google, and roles control which modules each person sees.

sections.heading: Details
points: Project Master is one company-wide list of projects and floors, used by every module.
Project Schedule is an MS Project-style schedule with activity links.
Hindrance Register records site hindrances and delays against projects and activities.
Quantity Sheet tracks baselines and monthly quantities by floor.
New users sign in as guests with access to the Report Transformer only.

title: Quantity Sheet
summary: Quantity sheet with theoretical consumption logic.

title: New web app
summary: The report tool became a web app, with a Flutter front end and a FastAPI backend.

title: Report Transformer
summary: ERP activity, material and labour reports are turned into formatted Excel sheets.
